Your objective is to MAXIMIZE the reaction yield — the percentage of the limiting substrate converted to the desired coupled product.

You control the following parameters (each with its physical role and allowed range):

  - res_time — residence time (range [60, 600] s): how long reagents spend in the reactor — longer allows more conversion but also more catalyst decomposition and side-reactions

turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning

**Ligand choice:** L3 is clearly the standout. It holds most of the top results: 98.7% (189 s, 110 °C, 2.51 mol%), 91.3%, 83.9%, 83.1%, 80.2%. L6 is second-best (85.4%, 81.3%), but L3's best results dominate. L5 is essentially dead (<10% everywhere), and L0/L1/L2/L4 top out in the 40–70% range.

**Temperature:** Every yield above ~30% occurs at 110 °C; low temperatures give near-zero yield regardless of ligand. The catalyst (with L3 at least) evidently tolerates 110 °C over these timescales, so set temperature to the maximum: **110 °C**.

**Catalyst loading:** With L3 at 110 °C, high loading (~2.51 mol%) at short residence time gave the best results (83.9%, 98.7%), while ~1.1–1.3 mol% needed the full 600 s to reach 72–91%. Higher loading accelerates conversion enough to finish before decomposition/side-reactions matter. Use near-maximum: **2.51 mol%**.

**Residence time:** At full loading and 110 °C, ~190 s gave 98.7% and ~200 s gave 83.9% — conversion is essentially complete around 190–200 s. Going much longer (600 s) at high loading was not tested for L3, and long times risk catalyst decomposition and side-product formation (consistent with L2: 62.8% at 185 s vs. lower-loading long runs performing worse). Staying near the observed optimum is safest, with a tiny extension to ensure full conversion: **~200 s**.

# Final Answer

**Final: ligand=L3, res_time=195, temperature=110, catalyst_loading=2.515**
